title: Account for client-side prompt rewrites and server post-processing in streaming metering pipeline
creator: Ava Chen
description: Background: Customers (and internal SDKs) sometimes rewrite prompts locally for privacy (PII redaction), macro expansion, or instruction templating. Separately, the server runtime may apply post-processing steps (truncate-to-max-tokens, deterministic de-dup, sampling-normalization) before final tokenization for billing. Problem: the current metering pipeline attributes token costs to the raw client payload length or to the immediately tokenized input without deterministic reconciliation after rewrites and post-processing. This causes two recurring classes of errors: 1) underbilling when server post-processing expands tokens (e.g., macro expansion occurs after a cheap client-side placeholder) and 2) overbilling when client-side truncation or normalization reduces tokens but the server previously reserved credits. Goal: create deterministic, auditable accounting for tokens and quota checks when client-side rewrites and server post-processing occur in streaming flows (including mid-stream rewriters, on-resume transformations, and post-finalization edits).
acceptance_criteria: Metering ledger always reconciles to a single canonical token provenance chain for each request and streaming session: original client bytes -> effective post-processed bytes -> final tokenized blocks used for billing

Edge cases covered by automated tests: mid-stream client rewrite (insert/delete), server-side expansion (macro/template replacement), resume-after-rewrite using websocket reconnects, and aborted sessions with partial responses
No customer sees a sustained >0.1% discrepancy between observed token charges and deterministic re-tokenization in audit replay tests across sampled production traffic
New metrics available in Console: rewrite_expansions/sec, rewrite_reductions/sec, mismatch_reconciliations, and retrospective_adjustments (count and value) with per-customer breakdown
Design reviewed by Security and PM; rollout plan staged with feature flag and canary across 1%/10%/50%/100% capacity
Documentation updated: billing model doc, SDK changelog, and public FAQ explaining when retrospective adjustments can occur
design_notes: Introduce a canonicalization step at the ingress boundary that records a small immutable delta record for any client-side rewrite detected by SDK or gateway. Delta record format: [op: insert|delete|replace, byte_range, replacement_hash, reason_tag]. These are immutable metadata used for provenance but not for billing by themselves.

Move final billing tokenization to a deterministic component after all post-processing is complete. The runtime will emit a tokenization fingerprint (model+tokenizer+seeded-config) and per-chunk token counts which the metering ledger stores atomically with the request finalization event.

For streaming flows: preserve ordered checkpoints. Each checkpoint contains the cumulative canonicalized byte-length and cumulative token count. On reconnect or resume, we diff last checkpoint vs new stream start to compute delta tokens owed or to credit refunds. This avoids double counting when clients resend but the server de-duplicates by checkpoint-hash.

Retrospective adjustments: when server-side expansion increases token count beyond preliminary reservation, we charge an adjustment event rather than recharging the original request. Similarly, when client truncation or suppression reduces tokens after initial reservation, we issue a credit event. All adjustments are idempotent and carry provenance links to the checkpoint IDs.

Security note: replacement_hash must be a SHA256 over the replacement bytes but never include raw PII; SDKs should hash substituted tokens client-side before sending delta metadata if privacy mode is enabled.

We will keep the existing fast-path that estimates upfront credit for latency-sensitive requests but mark those as provisional; finalization will update the ledger atomically. Customers will see provisional charges in UI flagged until finalized (within 10s for most flows).

Implement reconcile worker to generate retrospective adjustments and expose adjustment API (billing team)
End-to-end tests: create simulated clients with rewrites, server-side macros, reconnect/resume scenarios (qa and eng)
Instrument metrics and dashboards in Console and build alerting for mismatch_reconciliations (observability)
Documentation: public billing doc, SDK changelog, and internal runbook for dispute resolution (doc owner)

Canary rollout gating and feature flagging (infra/ops)
Ship SDK updates (minor semver) with backwards compatibility handling for older clients

comments: 2026-03-01 Ava Chen: Created initial ticket after customer support case #CS-1832 where a customer observed a 2x token variance between SDK-local estimate and invoice. Assigned to Diego for implementation planning.

2026-03-03 Diego Martinez: Spike complete. Confirmed two root causes: (1) SDK macro expansion performed after client-side token estimate; (2) server-side deterministic de-dup during streaming finalization that changed token boundaries. Recorded PoC for checkpoint checksums.
2026-03-05 Design review: Team agreed on preserving immutable delta metadata and moving to atomic finalization. Security requested hashed replacement values and a privacy-mode flag.

2026-03-07 Diego Martinez: Implemented metering ledger schema migration in branch feat/metering-checkpoints. Unit tests added for atomic finalization. Draft PR: github.com/redwood-inference/metering/pull/89

2026-03-10 QA: Found replay-case where client reconnects and replays an earlier chunk with different rewrite metadata; created additional logic to prefer server-side checkpoint-hash over client-supplied sequence numbers to dedupe. Updated tests to include varying rewrite fingerprints.
2026-03-12 PM (Jordan Patel): Approved canary plan. Will start with 1% of Hosted API traffic, monitor mismatch_reconciliations and retrospective_adjustments, then expand to 10% if metrics stable.

2026-03-13 Diego Martinez: Open items: finalize SDK spec for delta records and add observability span to map checkpoints to invoice events. Planning to submit core PRs this week and schedule security review next Tues.
